gaps.sentence: I've told you everything ___ you need to know.
gaps.explanation: After 'everything', 'that' is used (and may be omitted); 'which' is avoided after 'everything'.

gaps.sentence: Tell me ___ you said to her.
gaps.explanation: 'What you said' means 'the words that you said'; 'that' cannot head the clause after 'me'.

gaps.sentence: The discussion got to a stage ___ nobody was listening any more.
gaps.explanation: 'A stage where ...' means 'a stage at which ...'; the clause has its own subject and verb, so 'which' is impossible.

gaps.hint: after 'all', the relative pronoun is not 'what'
gaps.explanation: 'All that glitters' is the proverb pattern; 'what' cannot follow 'all', and 'which' is avoided after 'all'.

gaps.sentence: She was two hours late, ___ annoyed the interviewer.
gaps.hint: comment on the whole situation before the comma
gaps.explanation: When a clause comments on the whole previous statement, use 'which' after the comma.

gaps.sentence: Have you met the couple ___ son is in your class?
gaps.hint: the son belongs to the couple
gaps.explanation: 'Whose son' means 'their son'; the possessive relative 'whose' is required.

gaps.sentence: She told me ___ had happened, but I didn't believe her.
gaps.explanation: 'What had happened' means 'the things that had happened'; 'that' cannot stand alone as the subject here.

gaps.sentence: The author, about ___ there has been much debate, will speak at the festival.
gaps.hint: debate about the author — person after preposition
gaps.explanation: 'About whom' is required after the preposition 'about' when referring to a person.
